meta.note: Generated 2026-09-26 by an earlier ad-hoc script with ensemble context, on the saved plan of the matching legacy-noctx run, BEFORE the written-pitch-chord change; git SHA not recorded. Parts written one at a time in voice order, each hearing the finished parts.

plan.melodySummary: The melody journeys from a warm French Horn statement through the violins, dipping into the Cello for a tender middle passage before Clarinet and Violin 1 carry it to a soaring fortissimo climax, then settling back to Violin 1 for the resolution. The dynamic arc rises from an intimate !p! opening through successive espressivo swells, peaks at !ff! in mm.19-24, and gently subsides to a lingering !p! close.

sections.label: Phrase A — First Statement
sections.notes: Sing the tune !p! espressivo, broad and noble; linger slightly on the phrase-end half notes of m.4 and m.6, letting the tone bloom above the hushed strings.

sections.label: Phrase A' — Violins Take Over
sections.notes: Take the melody !mp! with a warm hairpin into each downbeat; a gentle ritenuto feeling on the A,4 of m.12 before the next phrase presses forward.

sections.label: Phrase B — Tender Middle (Cello lead)
sections.notes: Cello sings out !mf! on the A-string, richly vibrant; shape mm.13-16 with a swelling hairpin, then hand the register up as the octave-higher continuation begins in m.17.

sections.label: Phrase C — Climb to the Climax
sections.notes: Drive the line !f! crescendo to !ff! at the m.24 climax; broad, brilliant tone, pressing through the Bm color in m.23 with a secondary-dominant lean into the cadence.

sections.label: Phrase D — Fervent High Point
sections.notes: Blaze the tune !ff! at full stretch, then begin a long diminuendo through m.30; grand espressivo bowing, easing back as the phrase relaxes toward the close.

sections.label: Coda — Gentle Resolution
sections.notes: Settle to !p! with a tender ritardando into the final d6; let the tied whole-note sustain softly as the ensemble resolves the D chord beneath it.

Violin 1.instruction: Principal lyric voice: espressivo with generous vibrato, shaping every phrase with !p!→!f!→!p! hairpins; carry the climactic mm.25-30 at !ff! then draw back to a hushed !p! close, always the loudest line when you hold the melody.

Violin 2.instruction: Flowing arpeggios and gently repeated inner chords beneath the tune; weave chromatic suspensions that resolve downward, staying one dynamic step under the melody carrier throughout.

Clarinet.instruction: Warm countermelody and inner color most of the piece with singing legato; take the lead in mm.19-24, cresc. !f!→!ff! into the climax, projecting clearly above all accompaniment.

French Horn.instruction: Open the work as the noble melodic voice at !p! espressivo; thereafter sustain rich harmonic pedals and warm countermelodic fragments, always yielding dynamically to whoever holds the tune.

Cello.instruction: Provide a flowing arpeggiated bass and chromatic countermelody elsewhere; in mm.13-18 sing the melody !mf! on the upper strings with expressive vibrato, standing above the supporting voices.
